analysis.title: GS DeGrasse - GS Financials & REITs Sector Specialist: Week 1 down .. on to week 2
key_insights: Financials and REITs both gained about 1-2% last week and outperformed as the market broadened out from the tech trade.

Winners across Financials and REITs fell into three groups: defensive (P&C Insurance, Exchanges, Healthcare REITs), consumer-exposed (Payments with capital-light models ahead of balance-sheet fintechs, Lodging and Retail REITs), and Information services, which diverged from the more consensus-long Software names.
Laggards overlapped with cyclical exposure (Industrial REITs, Banks) or Capital Markets (Alts, Investment Banks and money centers).
Fundamental investors were frustrated that price action was driven by macro. Some preferred longs showed solid follow-through across choppy tapes, such as BLK and, to a lesser extent, MRSH and BNY.

Most debated earnings last week: TFC (PPNR versus PT income, and whether it is becoming a story stock) and SCHW (funding and balance sheet certainty, NNA outlook better than expected). SCHW feedback was high but tilted bearish.

Feedback tilted exceptionally bullish and the stocks worked for BLK, MRSH and BNY. RF went the opposite way (negative feedback, stock outperformed). IBKR and C had bullish feedback but performance did not align. PGR had bearish feedback and performance aligned.

Other inbound questions: TRV (do fundamentals matter or is pricing too socialized), FHN (does the sale change M&A optionality), wealth getting more competitive, election implications, regional banks versus money centers, what gets alts working again, what drives Lodging outperformance, C underperformance, tower REIT upside case, annuity surrender risk, and datacenters in Alt portfolios (with added focus on insurance).

BX next week: hedge funds want to be long the alts and the market will likely look for green shoots for the group. Incremental concern has crept in on datacenters and on more speculative assets and credits. Bulls cite BX's leverage to the datacenter theme. Bears focus on pace of management fee growth, BREIT recovery and BREP fundraising given higher rates, and AI slowdown concerns.

AXP next week: the agentic commerce debate featuring AXP cardmember services is not expected to resolve at earnings. Bulls point to an improving top line into year end. Views are mixed on VCE. Bears see less opex flexibility given recent headlines, while bulls believe the risk and controls investment is already in the run rate.

NTRS next week: trust bank flows have been active since STT reported. The crowd is more cautious than on peers, focused on expense and Investments commentary and potential diverging revenue trends among peers.

CBRE next week: focus is on the guide and whether higher rates have paused or broken pipelines. Feedback on brokers over the past month has been bearish (slower 4Q guide that could leak into 2027 numbers), but hedge funds are less inclined to stay short CBRE into earnings. GS GIR (Julien) calls CBRE approaching trough on trough, and desk flows in CBRE have picked up and turned more positive.

WTFC, EWBC and BPOP are getting more attention as potential beneficiaries of the higher rate environment. Banks with CRE and multifamily exposure are viewed with extra caution (FLG and OZK report next week), on both credit and NIM.

FCNCA: focus on whether it realizes its asset sensitivity (funding costs as the FDIC note winds down), expense estimates for next year, and M&A. FITB: bullish views on efficiency and NIM near and medium term, with caution on capital given the rate move.

LAZ: positioning is 1/10 and most do not expect resolution or clarity on margin yet. MSCI: expectations for new subscriptions look low relative to the bullish tone last quarter, but investors like being long into the setup (positioning score 6/10).

GS Prime: Financials were net sold (-1.2 SDs over 1 year), with short sales outpacing long buys 4.4 to 1. Capital Markets (especially Asset Managers and Data Services), Insurance, and Transaction and Payment Processing were the most net sold subsectors. Consumer Finance and Banks were modestly net bought.
